response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.total) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_diff FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Only customers with at least one invoice are counted as 'customers' when computing the average share (customers with no invoices are excluded).
Multiplying by 1.0 forces decimal division so shares are not truncated to integers; no rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every customer in the Customer table, treating customers with no invoices as having a total of 0 and a share of 0, which lowers the average share.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.total) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_diff FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
